findings.title: Boolean contract antecedent still compares the null-tested value with NULL by equality
findings.problem: The change moved NullEqualityVisitor (lines 528, 531) from `Nullness.NULL.equals(...)` to `isNull()`, but the boolean-antecedent path still checks `antecedentNullness.equals(targetNullness)` with antecedentNullness `NULL`. Inside `if (v == null)` a wildcard read `v` is now `NULL_NO_CHANGE` instead of `NULL`, so for `f(null == v, w)` with `@Contract("true, null -> false")` the satisfied first argument is no longer skipped, the clause sees two unknown arguments, is dropped as unsupported, and `w` is not refined. Master refined `w`; the head reports a dereference of `w` in the then-branch, while the same code with a plain `@Nullable Object v` is still accepted.

evidence.text: Probe correctness-probes/CorrectnessProbeTests.java, method contractNullFirstInsideNullTest: on head it reports `Test.java:13: dereferenced expression 'w' is @Nullable` (the wildcard variant) and nothing at line 19 (the plain `@Nullable Object v` variant) (correctness-probes/head-results.xml); on base 13392cb8 the method passes with no diagnostic (correctness-probes/base-results.xml).

ContractHandler.java:391-392: `Nullness targetNullness = inputs.valueOfSubNode(nullTestTarget);` / `if (antecedentNullness.equals(targetNullness)) {`; antecedentNullness is only ever `Nullness.NULL` or `Nullness.NONNULL` (lines 386-390).
The change rewrote the sibling tests at ContractHandler.java:528 and 531 to `if (lhsNullness.isNull())` / `if (rhsNullness.isNull())`.

AccessPathNullnessPropagation.java:543-546 sets the equal branch of `v == null` to `leftVal.greatestLowerBound(...)`, which for a NO_CHANGE `v` and NULL is NULL_NO_CHANGE; `Nullness.isNull()` is true for NULL and NULL_NO_CHANGE.

findings.proposed_solution: At ContractHandler.java:392 compare by meaning: treat the argument as satisfied when `antecedentNullness == NULL ? targetNullness.isNull() : targetNullness == NONNULL`, as lines 528 and 531 already do for the null comparison, and add the `f(null == v, w)` case with a wildcard-read `v` inside `if (v == null)` to the contract tests, expecting no report.

findings.title: Lambda argument returns a NO_CHANGE value into a non-null-bounded method type variable unreported
findings.problem: For a lambda passed as an argument, lambdaTypeAtTarget takes the return target from javac's parameter type at the call (getParameterTarget(...).type()) and drops the ValueTarget's excludesNull flag. With `static <U> void take(Sup<U> s)` (U has a non-null bound), javac substitutes U := T, so `take(() -> box.get())` on a `Box<? extends T>` with `T extends @Nullable Object` returns into a plain `T` and is accepted. The same value passed directly to `static <U> void takeValue(U u)` is still reported, because getParameterTarget excludes null for a parameter whose declared type is a type variable with a non-null bound. Master reported the lambda call (an inference failure on U); the head reports nothing, so a value that is null whenever T is instantiated with a nullable type now reaches a consumer whose U requires non-null. This is the rule the description states for parameters ("a nullable upper bound on that type variable"), not applied to the lambda path, and it is not one of the agreed follow-ups, which concern new reports, not missed ones. Severity is minor because the lambda path already accepts a plain `T` value there (`take(() -> t)` is unreported on master too); the change extends that gap to wildcard reads and makes the lambda and direct-argument paths disagree for them.

evidence.text: Probe correctness-probes/CorrectnessProbeTests.java, method lambdaVsDirectNonNullBound, run on head fc9b07b3 with JDK 21: `./gradlew --quiet :nullaway:test --tests com.uber.nullaway.jspecify.CorrectnessProbeTests`. Head reports only `Test.java:16: passing @Nullable parameter 'box.get()' where @NonNull is required` (direct `takeValue(box.get())`) and line 19 (`take(() -> null)`); lines 10 `take(() -> box.get());` and 13 `take(() -> { return box.get(); });` get no diagnostic (correctness-probes/head-results.xml).

The same probe on base 13392cb8 reports `Test.java:10` and `Test.java:13: inference failure: type variable U is constrained to be @Nullable, but its upper bound requires it to be @NonNull` (correctness-probes/base-results.xml).

NullAway.java:1399-1408 reads only `.type()` of `genericsChecks.getParameterTarget(callee, call, formalParamType, ...)`, where formalParamType comes from `invokedMethodTypeAtCall` (javac's substituted type); GenericsChecks.java:5000-5002 computes the excludes-null flag from `declaredType instanceof Type.TypeVar && !GenericsUtils.upperBoundIsNullable(...)`, which only fires when the parameter itself is a type variable, not a type argument of the functional interface.

The same probe's `viaLambdaParam`, `take(() -> t)` with a parameter `T t` (Test.java:22), gets no diagnostic on base 13392cb8 or on head (correctness-probes/base-results.xml, head-results.xml): the lambda path already accepted a plain `T` value into a non-null-bounded `U` before this change, so the head extends an existing gap to wildcard reads rather than opening a new one.

findings.proposed_solution: Make the lambda return target exclude null when the functional interface's return type comes from a method type variable of the callee whose upper bound is non-null (for example, map the lambda's return type back through the callee's declared parameter type `Sup<U>` and apply the same bound test getParameterTarget applies to a type-variable parameter), and add the `take(() -> box.get())` case with `<U>` (non-null bound) to NullnessOperatorTests as a reported case next to its direct-argument twin.

findings.title: Lambda return target recomputed beside the poly-expression type GenericsChecks already keeps
findings.problem: GenericsChecks already computes the functional interface type of a lambda passed as an argument, with the nullness its target supplies, and stores it in inferredPolyExpressionTypes; getPolyExpressionType returns it. The new NullAway.lambdaTypeAtTarget computes the same type a second way: it walks to the parent call, iterates InvocationArguments over javac's method type, and builds the parameter type through getParameterTarget, which takes the receiver's member type but skips NullAway's inference of method type arguments and the handler and PolyNull models that getInvokedMethodTypeAtCall applies. checkReturnExpression now reads both for one lambda return: getPolyExpressionType for the @Nullable-return bail-out and lambdaTypeAtTarget for the NO_CHANGE decision. Where the two types differ, for example a generic method whose type variable NullAway infers as @NonNull T from another argument, the lambda path accepts a NO_CHANGE return that the direct-argument path reports (the PR description lists `two(box.get(), "x")` and `Holder.make(t, ts).set(box.get())` as reported because of that inference). The generics-specific target typing also lives in NullAway.java, a 3600-line file, rather than in GenericsChecks next to the cache it duplicates, so a later fix to one of the two lambda typings will not reach the other.

evidence.text: NullAway.java:1464 `Type lambdaType = genericsChecks.getPolyExpressionType(lambdaTree);` and NullAway.java:1477 `() -> returnTargetAtReturn(methodSymbol, lambdaTree, state),` in the same checkReturnExpression; returnTargetAtReturn calls `lambdaTypeAtTarget(lambdaTree, state)` at NullAway.java:1348.

NullAway.java:1394 `new InvocationArguments(call, invokedMethodTypeAtCall(call, callee))` uses javac's method type (NullAway.java:3224-3233), then NullAway.java:1416 `GenericsUtils.groundTargetType(targets.get(0), state, config, handler)`; the PR makes groundTargetType public for this caller (GenericsUtils.java diff).

GenericsChecks.java:1541-1558 already stores, for each lambda argument, `GenericsUtils.groundTargetType(formalParamType, ...)` with inferred nullability into `inferredPolyExpressionTypes.put(argument, typeWithInferredNullability)`, and maybeStorePolyExpressionTypeFromTarget (GenericsChecks.java ~5012) stores the grounded target type from the formal parameter of getInvokedMethodTypeAtCall, which applies memberType of the receiver, NullAway inference, handler.onOverrideMethodType, and the PolyNull model (GenericsChecks.java:3914-3943).

getParameterTarget (GenericsChecks.java:4955) builds the type from `TypeSubstitutionUtils.memberType(..., receiverType, methodSymbol, config)` or `methodSymbol.type` and javac's formalParamType, with no inference and no handler model, so for a static generic method the lambda target keeps the unannotated method type variable that NullAway's inference may have made @NonNull.

findings.proposed_solution: Move the lambda target typing into GenericsChecks and derive it from the type that getPolyExpressionType already returns for the lambda (fixing the cache where it lacks the receiver-supplied annotations), so checkReturnExpression reads one functional interface type for both the @Nullable bail-out and the NO_CHANGE decision; if the uninferred type is intended for NO_CHANGE, say why in lambdaTypeAtTarget's Javadoc and add a test with a lambda argument whose method type variable NullAway infers from another argument.

findings.title: No test shows a lambda argument accepted through parentheses, a body-less constructor, or a later varargs position
findings.problem: The description and the Javadoc of lambdaTypeAtTarget claim that a lambda passed as an argument of a call, or of a constructor with no class body, returns into the type of the receiving parameter, that parentheses around the lambda are skipped, and that an anonymous-class constructor argument returns into a target that excludes null. issue1727LambdaReturnFalsePositive, the only test that reaches this method, checks the parenthesized, constructor, anonymous-class, and varargs forms only against parameters of type Box<@NonNull U>, where the expected report also appears when the method returns null and the lambda falls back to EXCLUDES_NULL. findings.title: Five coined words for the target of a pseudo-assignment, plus "moves" for the assignment itself
findings.problem: The change names one concept, the variable, parameter, return, or array element that a value is assigned, passed, or returned to, with five words: "target" (`ValueTarget`, `holderTarget`), "location" (`locationOf`, "the location that receives"), "holder" (`holder` parameters, `valueHeldAs`, `valueHeldByPath`, "moves to a holder"), "sink" ("Every sink", "the sinks use"), and "destination" ("supplies the destination"). The operation itself is called "moves" ("once it moves to a holder", "node whose value moves", "dataflow moves it to"), a metaphor for assignment, argument passing, return, and an array store. The codebase at the base already has the words: "pseudo-assignment" and `nonNullTarget` in `ErrorBuilder`, and the change's own Javadoc on `Nullness.NO_CHANGE` lists "an assignment, an argument, a return, or an array store". A reader of the public `Nullness.withoutNoChange()` Javadoc cannot tell that "moves to a holder" means a pseudo-assignment, or that "holder", "location", and "sink" are the same thing as a `ValueTarget`; grepping for any one word finds a fraction of the uses. Open threads already ask for "assigned location" and "pseudo-assignment" in `acceptsNoChangeValue` (GenericsChecks.java:4811) and for new names of `valueHeldByPath` and `valueHeldAs`; the same coinages also sit in `Nullness.java`, `NullAway.java`, `holderTarget`, `locationOf`, and their Javadoc, which those threads do not reach.

findings.title: Config Javadoc says every read through a nullable-bounded type variable is NO_CHANGE
findings.problem: The Javadoc of `handleWildcardGenerics()` says the option computes `NO_CHANGE` "for a value read through a type variable with a nullable upper bound". Read literally, that covers `List<T>.get()`, a parameter of type `T`, and a field of type `T`, and a reader of the public `Config` interface will expect those to become `NO_CHANGE` with the option on. The `Nullness.NO_CHANGE` Javadoc says the opposite: only a read through a wildcard or capture bounded by `T`, and an enhanced-for element of type `T`, gets `NO_CHANGE`; `List<T>.get()` stays `NONNULL`. The two comments in one change disagree on which values the option affects.

evidence.text: Config.java:319-322: "These also compute {@link Nullness#NO_CHANGE} for a value read through a type variable with a nullable upper bound, such as the result of {@code Box<? extends T>.get()} or an enhanced-for element of type {@code T}"

Nullness.java:59-66: "NullAway gives this nullness to a value read through a wildcard or capture bounded by {@code T} ... Any other value of type {@code T}, such as a parameter, a field, or the result of {@code List<T>.get()}, is {@link #NONNULL}"

findings.proposed_solution: Name the same cases `Nullness.NO_CHANGE` names: "These also compute `NO_CHANGE` for a value read through a wildcard or capture bounded by a type variable with a nullable upper bound, such as the result of `Box<? extends T>.get()`, and for an enhanced-for element of type `T`; any other value of type `T`, such as the result of `List<T>.get()`, stays `NONNULL`." Or link to `Nullness#NO_CHANGE` for the list instead of restating it.

findings.title: Handler contract on set positions names no case where setting NONNULL changes the result
findings.problem: The new paragraph on the public extension point says that a position a handler sets to `NONNULL`, "even to the value it already holds", "requires a non-null argument whatever the parameter's type". A handler author cannot tell from this what differs between a position left at the base analysis's `NONNULL` and one set to `NONNULL`, since both read `NONNULL`, nor which argument is affected. The case is a `NO_CHANGE` argument, such as `box.get()` on a `Box<? extends T>`, passed to a parameter of type `T`: left alone, the parameter accepts it; set by a handler, the parameter is treated as `ValueTarget.EXCLUDES_NULL` and the call is reported. Nothing in the paragraph names `NO_CHANGE`, a `T` parameter, or the report, so a handler that copies every position through (a pattern the old contract allowed) silently starts producing reports.

evidence.text: Handler.java:235-237: "A position that a handler sets, even to the value it already holds, is that handler's decision: NONNULL there requires a non-null argument whatever the parameter's type, so a handler sets only the positions it decides."

NullAway.java:2614-2622: the target is `varArgsPassedAsArray || finalArgumentNullness.wasSet(paramIndex) ? GenericsChecks.ValueTarget.EXCLUDES_NULL : genericsChecks.getParameterTarget(...)`, so `wasSet` only matters for a value `isTopLevelNullnessCompatible` passes to the target supplier, which its Javadoc (NullAway.java:3246-3248) says happens only for a value for which `isNoChange()` holds
A handler that calls `set(i, get(i))` for every position marks each one as set, so a `NO_CHANGE` argument to a `T` parameter it does not model is reported where it was accepted before

findings.proposed_solution: State the case in the paragraph, for example: "Where a handler leaves a position unset, a parameter whose type is a type variable `T` still accepts a value for which `Nullness#isNoChange()` holds, such as `box.get()` on a `Box<? extends T>`. A position the handler sets to `NONNULL`, even to the value it already holds, rejects that value too. Set only the positions the handler models."

findings.title: HandleWildcardGenerics wiki entry omits the enhanced-for type-variable case the option now gates
findings.problem: The change widens what `-XepOpt:NullAway:HandleWildcardGenerics` controls: it now also decides how NullAway treats an enhanced-for element whose type is a type variable `T` with a nullable upper bound (`NO_CHANGE` with the option on, non-null as in 0.14.0 with it off). The option's only reference entry, the Configuration page of the NullAway wiki, still says the option covers 'wildcard generic types' and nothing else. A user who hits the vavr-style `for (T t : this)` reports, or who wants the 0.14.0 behavior back, finds no hint on that page that this option is the switch, and the JSpecify Support page links to the same entry as 'checking and inference for wildcard types'.

evidence.text: uber/NullAway.wiki origin/master Configuration.md:324: "Within JSpecify mode, enables improved support for nullability checking and type inference involving wildcard generic types."

nullaway/src/main/java/com/uber/nullaway/generics/GenericsChecks.java:4647-4657 returns `Nullness.NO_CHANGE` for a `Type.TypeVar` with a non-`NONNULL` upper bound only when `config.handleWildcardGenerics()` is true; otherwise the read is `NONNULL`.

PR description: "The option now also covers an enhanced-for element whose type is a type variable `T`; #1786 already gated wildcard element types." and "With `HandleWildcardGenerics` off, an enhanced-for variable of type `T`, where `T` has a nullable upper bound, is non-null as in 0.14.0".
No page in the repository documents the option: README.md and the other tracked .md files contain no `HandleWildcardGenerics` or `wildcard` mention; the wiki is the record.
The wiki is a separate repository, so the entry cannot be updated in this PR's diff; it is owed alongside the release that ships the change.

findings.proposed_solution: Extend the Handle Wildcard Generics entry on the wiki Configuration page (in the release that ships this change) with one sentence: the option also governs values read through a type variable with a nullable upper bound, such as `box.get()` on a `Box<? extends T>` or an enhanced-for element of type `T`; with it on they are accepted where `T` is expected and reported at a dereference, with it off an enhanced-for element of type `T` is treated as non-null.

findings.title: followUnsubstitutedTypeVarUpperBound is still documented as using the upper bound
findings.problem: The change makes this flag do something different, but its @param line and the summary sentence still describe the old behavior. Before the change, true meant that for an unsubstituted type variable the method returned the nullness of its upper bound, so `T extends @Nullable Object` gave NULLABLE. Now true makes the method return NO_CHANGE for such a T when HandleWildcardGenerics is on, and NONNULL when it is off. The bound's own nullness is never returned. The @return line was updated and the @param line was not, so the two now contradict each other. A reader who goes by the @param line expects true to give NULLABLE for a nullable-bounded T. The maintainer's open question on the one-flag overload (why that overload can return NO_CHANGE when it passes false) comes from the same unclear definition of the flag.

evidence.text: GenericsChecks.java:4609-4610 (unchanged): "Returns the nullness of a value read from {@code type}, optionally following the upper bound of an unsubstituted type variable." GenericsChecks.java:4616-4617 (unchanged): "@param followUnsubstitutedTypeVarUpperBound whether to use the upper bound when {@code type} is an unsubstituted type variable"

Base 13392cb8 body: `if (followUnsubstitutedTypeVarUpperBound && type instanceof Type.TypeVar typeVar) { ... return getTypeNullnessForRead(upperBound, ..., true); }`, which returns the bound's nullness. Head GenericsChecks.java:4647-4658: `if (config.handleWildcardGenerics() && followUnsubstitutedTypeVarUpperBound && type instanceof Type.TypeVar typeVar && !getTypeNullnessForRead(typeVar.getUpperBound(), ...).equals(Nullness.NONNULL)) { return Nullness.NO_CHANGE; } return Nullness.NONNULL;`
The new @return line at GenericsChecks.java:4618-4621 says NO_CHANGE with the option on and NONNULL with it off, which contradicts "use the upper bound" in the @param line above it.
The flag still decides whether the upper bound of an unsubstituted type variable is consulted, so the @param is stale rather than wrong; the @return line two lines below states the new result.

findings.proposed_solution: Reword the @param line and the summary to the flag's current meaning. For example, the @param could read: whether an unsubstituted type variable whose upper bound may be null reads as NO_CHANGE (with HandleWildcardGenerics on) rather than NONNULL. Consider renaming the flag to match, and answer the open thread with the corrected definition.

findings.title: Only the Before twin of the non-null receiver-field getters is deprecated
findings.problem: The change adds the same pair of initialization getters for both program points (`getInitializedFieldsOfReceiverBefore` and `getInitializedFieldsOfReceiverAtExit`), but deprecates only `getNonnullFieldsOfReceiverBefore`; `getNonnullFieldsOfReceiverAtExit` stays undeprecated. Both old methods still return exactly what their names say (fields holding `NONNULL`), so the Before method is not wrong; it is deprecated only because its last in-tree caller moved. A handler author who reads the two pairs as twins gets a deprecation warning on one and not the other, and the warning on a method that still gives a non-null guarantee points to one that, by its own Javadoc, gives none. The PR description explains why AtExit stays (`@EnsuresNonNull` uses it) but not why Before, the same query at a different point, is retired.

evidence.text: AccessPathNullnessAnalysis.java:223-232: `@deprecated for an initialization check, use {@link #getInitializedFieldsOfReceiverBefore}, which also returns a field that holds a value for which {@link Nullness#isNoChange()} holds. Such a value may be null, so that method gives no non-null guarantee.` followed by `@Deprecated public Set<Element> getNonnullFieldsOfReceiverBefore(...)`, whose body still selects `NullnessStore::getNonNullReceiverFields`.

AccessPathNullnessAnalysis.java:166-175: `getNonnullFieldsOfReceiverAtExit` has no `@Deprecated` and also selects `NullnessStore::getNonNullReceiverFields`; its in-tree caller is EnsuresNonNullHandler.java:86.

PR description: `getNonnullFieldsOfReceiverAtExit`, which `@EnsuresNonNull` checking uses, still returns only fields holding a non-null value; the author's 2026-11-03 comment gives "no main-code callers left" as the reason for deprecating the Before method.

findings.proposed_solution: Treat the two non-null getters alike: either drop `@Deprecated` from `getNonnullFieldsOfReceiverBefore` and keep the pointer to `getInitializedFieldsOfReceiverBefore` as a plain Javadoc note for initialization checks, or state in its `@deprecated` text why a non-null query before an expression is retired while the same query at exit is kept.

findings.title: PR title omits the new reports for null-tested @Nullable-element array elements
findings.problem: The change to the read of a `@Nullable`-element array element (AccessPathNullnessPropagation.java:892) keeps a NULL fact that master turned into NONNULL, so JSpecify-mode code that dereferences such an element after `array[i] == null` or `array[i] = null` gets new reports unrelated to wildcard reads. The description lists it first under Breaking changes, but the PR title, which becomes the squash commit headline, names only `? extends T` and enhanced-for reads, so a reader bisecting a new array report from the log will not find it by the headline.

evidence.text: Master, AccessPathNullnessPropagation.java:886-890 (base 13392cb8): `if (accessPathNullness == Nullness.NULLABLE) { resultNullness = Nullness.NULLABLE; } else { resultNullness = Nullness.NONNULL; }`, so a NULL fact on an array element became NONNULL before this PR.
Head, AccessPathNullnessPropagation.java:892: `resultNullness = input.getRegularStore().getNullnessOfAccessPath(arrayAccessPath);`

PR description, Breaking changes: "an element of a `@Nullable`-element array that dataflow knows is null, after `array[i] == null` or `array[i] = null`, is reported wherever it is dereferenced ... Dataflow treated such an element as non-null." The PR title names only `? extends T` and enhanced-for reads.
The NO_CHANGE work needs only that a NO_CHANGE or NULL_NO_CHANGE fact survives the read; keeping master's NULL to NONNULL mapping for plain NULL would leave the wildcard fix intact.

AccessPathNullnessPropagation.java:892 must at least keep NO_CHANGE and NULL_NO_CHANGE, which master's `else { resultNullness = Nullness.NONNULL; }` would turn into NONNULL; the description already lists the plain-NULL consequence first under Breaking changes.

findings.proposed_solution: Mention the array-element reports in the PR title or keep them out of this change; splitting is not required.

findings.title: No test pins that a call declared non-null ignores a null fact on its access path
findings.problem: The rewrite of returnValueNullness keeps master's rule that a call whose return is non-null is NONNULL without consulting the store (`declaredNullness.equals(NONNULL) ? NONNULL : ...`). Replacing that test with false, so the store is consulted with a NONNULL default, survives the whole suite. A later edit that drops the shortcut would start reporting `s.get().hashCode()` inside `if (s.get() == null)` for a non-null getter, with no test failing.

evidence.text: measure/nullaway-pitest-diff-survivors.txt: AccessPathNullnessPropagation.java 1279 `declaredNullness.equals(NONNULL)` survived 'removed conditional - replaced equality check with false', reached by 797 tests.

Base: `} else if (node == null || methodReturnsNonNull.test(node) || (!Nullness.hasNullableAnnotation(...) && !genericReturnIsNullable(node))) { nullness = NONNULL; }`; head AccessPathNullnessPropagation.java:1274-1281 moves this into the declaredNullness branch.
Under the mutant, the then-branch of `if (s.get() == null)` reads the NULL fact for the zero-argument call path, so a dereference there is reported where master and the head report nothing.

findings.proposed_solution: Add a case with a non-null getter dereferenced inside `if (s.get() == null)`, expecting no report, to the existing tests of access paths for zero-argument calls, or say in the pull request that this behavior is deliberately left unpinned.

findings.title: Description states three outcomes twice, in the What paragraphs and again in the outcome lines
findings.problem: About 770 words of prose sit outside the outcome lines, and several paragraphs restate what a `User-visible:` or `Not changed:` line already carries, so the squash commit body says the same fact twice and a later edit can update one copy and not the other. The paragraph on handlers and `MethodParameterNullness` is also implementation detail the diff shows, and its only caller-visible fact is the `Not changed:` line about `onOverrideMethodInvocationParametersNullability`.

evidence.text: Paragraph "A handler that requires a non-null argument ... so the handler API holds only `NONNULL` and `NULLABLE` as before." duplicates the Not changed line "`Handler.onOverrideMethodInvocationParametersNullability` receives only `NONNULL`, `NULLABLE`, or `null` for a parameter, as before." and the line about "a parameter a library model marks non-null".

"Everywhere else the value stays nullable: a dereference, unboxing, an `Object` target, and a `@Contract` or `@EnsuresNonNull` postcondition." restates the first Not changed line (dereference, unboxing, `Object` target).

"Inside `if (value == null)` the value is `NULL_NO_CHANGE` ... a target of type `T` still accepts it ... After the test, the two branches join back to `NO_CHANGE`." restates the User-visible line "such a value is still accepted where `T` is expected after `if (value == null)`, inside the branch and after it"; "The option now also covers an enhanced-for element whose type is a type variable `T`" restates the `HandleWildcardGenerics` off line.

findings.proposed_solution: Drop the handler/`MethodParameterNullness` paragraph, the "Everywhere else the value stays nullable" sentence, and the restated acceptance and option-coverage clauses, keeping only the reason each mechanism exists (for example, that `NULL_NO_CHANGE` is the meet of `NULL` and `NO_CHANGE` so a dereference stays reported) where the outcome line does not give it.
